Band.why: Plausible 8 h band, but no dated public evidence and the scope is unfixed.

spike_plan.kill_if: Build needs network at run time, peaks above 16 GB, or exceeds about 2 hours of build time, or no non-Bazel path exists for the library.
spike_plan.pass_if: Offline build and one test binary from header-map and router tests complete within 16 GB and 8 cores, and results are identical across three runs.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container with at least 8 cores and 16 GB, check out envoy v1.40.0 at 2f6040e4 and install the Bazel version pinned in bazel/README.md.
Run bazel fetch for the header-map and router test targets only; record download size, wall time, and any pip or non-Bazel fetches.
Run bazel build of the header_map_impl_test and router header-formatter test targets on the cached repo; record peak RAM and time.
Disconnect the network (or use a fresh container with only the cache) and rerun the same build and one test binary; check that it still succeeds offline.

Check whether a non-Bazel build of the header/path library is possible (for example compiling source/common/http/header_map_impl.cc and path_utility.cc against abseil and protobuf headers) and whether it links.
Pick a small reproducible target (for example one test file) and confirm its output is deterministic over three runs.

v1.summary: Envoy v1.40.0 is a real, Apache-2.0 source with 85 relevant test files, so the paper trail is strong. The seed is killed as K7 because the Bazel-only build cannot yet be shown to run offline in the sandbox, and the subsystem to remove is still unspecified.
